summary_oneline: Instrument BedrockConverseBase.ask() with FEAT-397's per-round usage accumulation and ClientRoundEvent emission — one change that covers BedrockConverseClient and NovaClient, which inherits the loop verbatim.

localization.role: The single tool loop to instrument; already has _emit_before_call/_lc_tc (659) and _lc_t0 (667) in place
Where round counting, per-round CompletionUsage accumulation and per-round tool-name capture must be added; emission point is the end of the stopReason=='tool_use' branch at 800-807
Point after which the accumulated total overwrites ai_message.usage and extra_usage['rounds'] is stamped
Subclass of BedrockConverseBase that inherits ask() with no reimplementation — receives the fix for free
Thin BedrockConverseBase subclass — also receives the fix for free
Provider-agnostic emission primitive, already inherited by BedrockConverseBase — no change required
Existing Converse usage parser to reuse for each round's CompletionUsage
The accumulator; its shallow extra_usage merge is the source of the Bedrock cache-token hazard
Reference implementation to copy verbatim (init / accumulate / emit / stamp)
Sole runtime consumer of ClientRoundEvent; provider-agnostic, needs no change

Second, structurally identical tool loop (while True at 1063) — IN SCOPE per U2, but carries no lifecycle span today, so it needs _emit_before_call/_emit_after_call established before round events can attach
Streaming path with a single terminal usage payload; per-round streaming is a standing FEAT-397 non-goal
Nearest adjacent holdout — already accumulates manually, lacks only emission
Drives its own turn loop via _chat_completion, bypassing ask() — a separate per-round blind spot for all clients

constraints.statement: NovaClient inherits ask()/ask_stream()/invoke()/resume() from BedrockConverseBase with no reimplementation
constraints.implication: The change must be made on BedrockConverseBase, not on NovaClient or BedrockConverseClient; a Nova-specific implementation would be duplicate code and would drift

constraints.statement: _emit_round_event is defined on AbstractClient and short-circuits when neither the client-local nor the global registry has ClientRoundEvent subscribers
constraints.implication: No base-class or event-schema change is needed, and instrumentation is zero-cost when observability is off

constraints.statement: The five migrated clients emit ClientRoundEvent only inside the tool-use branch, so the final non-tool round produces no round event
constraints.implication: Bedrock must follow the same placement or its round counts will not be comparable with the other five clients in the same metrics

constraints.statement: CompletionUsage.__add__ shallow-merges extra_usage with right-hand-wins, while from_bedrock stores cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens there as first-class numbers
constraints.implication: Naive accumulation yields last-round-only cache counters on a multi-round call, contradicting ask()'s own docstring promise at bedrock.py:628-629

constraints.statement: extra_usage['rounds'] is set by the caller after the loop and only when round_number > 1
constraints.implication: Single-round Bedrock calls must remain byte-identical in behavior to today — the change must be a no-op for the non-tool path

constraints.statement: FEAT-397 established a one-file-per-client unit test convention (tests/unit/clients/test_<client>_multiround_usage.py) plus a single non-parametrized end-to-end test built around AnthropicClient
constraints.implication: A Bedrock test is a new file mirroring the convention, and the e2e test mocks a different SDK seam (_sdk_create, not _backend.build_client)

constraints.statement: MetricsSubscriber._on_client_round is the only runtime ClientRoundEvent consumer and is provider-agnostic
constraints.implication: No downstream/observability change is in scope; Bedrock rounds will flow into parrot.client.round.token.usage and parrot.client.rounds automatically

constraints.statement: AnthropicClient.resume() carries no FEAT-397 instrumentation, and per-round ask_stream() is an explicit FEAT-397 non-goal for every client
constraints.implication: Instrumenting Bedrock's resume()/ask_stream() would put Bedrock ahead of the reference clients and create a new asymmetry; parity argues for ask() only

constraints.statement: bedrock.py and nova/ have had no tool-loop refactor in 4 months; recent commits are credential and model-ID fixes
constraints.implication: Low conflict risk; the BedrockConverseBase extraction (TASK-1806) is precisely what makes the single-change approach viable

A NovaClient-specific test asserting the inherited path emits under client_name='nova' (the only Nova-specific surface, since the loop is shared)

patterns_to_follow: AnthropicClient.ask() four-part pattern: init accumulator (claude.py:533-535), accumulate per round (557-572), emit inside the tool_use branch (640-650), stamp the accumulated total after building the AIMessage (715-722) — evidence F003
Reuse CompletionUsage.from_bedrock (basic.py:147) and CompletionUsage.__add__ rather than hand-summing fields, unlike Gemma4Client's manual sum — evidence F005, F008
Round events fire with token fields None when the provider reported no usage for that round (base.py:544-546) — evidence F002, F001
integration_risks: Cache-token semantics: multi-round Bedrock calls would report last-round-only cacheRead/cacheWriteInputTokens under the current __add__ merge, silently contradicting the ask() docstring — evidence F005
Changing CompletionUsage.__add__ to sum numeric extra_usage keys would alter accumulated usage for all five already-migrated clients — cross-client blast radius, evidence F005

Bedrock's fallback path (_should_use_fallback at bedrock.py:742-749) issues a SECOND _sdk_create within the same iteration; round timing and usage must be attributed to the successful call, mirroring how claude.py handles its own fallback retry — evidence F003, F004

resume() IS in scope (U2), so Bedrock/Nova will report rounds that AnthropicClient.resume() does not — a deliberate, accepted asymmetry in the opposite direction that must be documented so it is not later 'fixed' by removal — evidence F006

resume() has NO lifecycle instrumentation whatsoever — no _emit_before_call, no _lc_tc, no _lc_t0, no _emit_after_call (they appear only in ask()). Per-round emission there first requires establishing a call-level span, so the resume() work is a strictly LARGER task than the ask() work and must be decomposed separately — evidence F010

confidence_map.statement: NovaClient inherits ask() from BedrockConverseBase, so instrumenting the base class covers BedrockConverseClient and NovaClient in one change
confidence_map.reasoning: Read directly: class NovaClient(BedrockConverseBase, ...) at nova/client.py:30, whose 121 lines define only __init__ and class attributes; the docstring states text methods are inherited with no reimplementation.

confidence_map.statement: BedrockConverseBase.ask() contains exactly one uninstrumented tool loop at bedrock.py:738-810 with the emission point at the end of the stopReason=='tool_use' branch
confidence_map.reasoning: Read the loop end-to-end; structure matches AnthropicClient's one-for-one.

confidence_map.statement: No change is required in base.py, metrics.py, or the ClientRoundEvent schema
confidence_map.reasoning: _emit_round_event takes only provider-neutral arguments and is defined on AbstractClient, which BedrockConverseBase subclasses; MetricsSubscriber._on_client_round consumes the event without provider branching.

confidence_map.statement: The FEAT-397 pattern is a stable four-part idiom replicated identically across five clients
confidence_map.reasoning: grep for _emit_round_event returns exactly five call sites plus the definition; grep for extra_usage['rounds'] returns the matching five stamp sites.

confidence_map.statement: CompletionUsage.from_bedrock already parses Converse usage and is reusable per round without new parsing code
confidence_map.reasoning: Read the classmethod; it is already called from BedrockConverseBase.invoke at bedrock.py:1208.

confidence_map.statement: Accumulating Bedrock rounds with CompletionUsage.__add__ leaves cacheRead/cacheWriteInputTokens at the last round's values instead of the sum
confidence_map.reasoning: __add__'s own docstring specifies shallow extra_usage merge with right-hand-wins, and from_bedrock places both counters in extra_usage; the two facts compose directly.

confidence_map.statement: Parity with the reference clients argues for scoping this to ask() and excluding resume() and ask_stream()
confidence_map.reasoning: The precedent is verified (AnthropicClient.resume has no instrumentation; ask_stream per-round is a written non-goal), but whether parity or completeness is the right objective for Bedrock is a product judgment the codebase cannot settle.

confidence_map.statement: Bedrock's in-loop fallback retry issues a second _sdk_create in the same iteration, requiring care in round timing and usage attribution
confidence_map.reasoning: The fallback branch is read directly at bedrock.py:742-749, but the correct attribution semantics are inferred from how claude.py structures its analogous retry rather than stated anywhere.

confidence_map.statement: Gemma4Client is the cheapest adjacent holdout — it already accumulates and lacks only event emission
confidence_map.reasoning: Its manual per-field sum is read at gemma4.py:542-546 and the FEAT-397 spec states the same, but the loop was surveyed by grep rather than read end-to-end.

confidence_map.statement: ClaudeAgentClient, TransformersClient and GeminiLiveClient each require a materially different design and do not belong in this feature
confidence_map.reasoning: Each was surveyed by targeted grep showing no client-side tool loop (ClaudeAgentClient, TransformersClient) or a separate usage type (GeminiLiveClient's LiveCompletionUsage), but none was read end-to-end.

confidence_map.statement: Instrumenting the Bedrock tool loop carries low merge-conflict risk
confidence_map.reasoning: Four months of history shows no tool-loop refactor, but git history cannot reveal uncommitted or unpushed work elsewhere.

confidence_map.statement: BedrockConverseBase.resume(), invoke() and ask_stream() have no lifecycle instrumentation at all; _emit_before_call/_lc_tc/_lc_t0 appear only in ask()
confidence_map.reasoning: Exhaustive grep of the three symbols across bedrock.py returns matches only at 659/667/854/857, all inside ask() (578-862).

confidence_map.statement: The LLMCodeDispatcher blind spot is orthogonal to this feature and will persist for Bedrock even after it ships
confidence_map.reasoning: The dispatcher's own turn loop calling client._chat_completion is read at dispatchers/llm.py:190 and 369-377, so it demonstrably bypasses ask(); the scoping conclusion is inference.

unknowns.question: For a multi-round Bedrock call, should cacheReadInputTokens/cacheWriteInputTokens be summed across rounds, or is last-round-wins acceptable?
plausible_answers: Sum them explicitly in the Bedrock loop after __add__ — correct totals, zero blast radius on other clients
Accept last-round-wins and document the limitation in the ask() docstring — smallest change
Teach CompletionUsage.__add__ to sum numeric extra_usage keys — most principled but changes accumulated usage for all five migrated clients
unknowns.user_answer: Sum them explicitly in the Bedrock loop after __add__. CompletionUsage.__add__ and models/basic.py stay UNTOUCHED — no cross-client blast radius.

unknowns.question: Should this feature stop at ask() for parity with the five reference clients, or also instrument BedrockConverseBase.resume()?
plausible_answers: ask() only — matches AnthropicClient exactly; record resume() as a carried-forward non-goal
ask() + resume() — Bedrock's resume() is a real tool loop and under-reporting rounds after a human-interaction suspend is a genuine observability hole
unknowns.user_answer: ask() + resume(). Both tool loops are instrumented. This deliberately puts Bedrock/Nova AHEAD of the five reference clients, whose resume() remains uninstrumented — the asymmetry is accepted, and closing it for the other clients is a follow-up.

unknowns.question: Should Gemma4Client be folded into this feature, given it already accumulates and needs only the emission call sites?
plausible_answers: No — keep FEAT-404 strictly Bedrock + Nova as requested; file Gemma4 separately
Yes — it is a few lines and closes three of the five FEAT-397 holdouts in one feature
unknowns.user_answer: No. FEAT-404 stays strictly Bedrock + Nova. Gemma4Client is filed as a follow-up alongside ClaudeAgentClient, TransformersClient and GeminiLiveClient.

recommended_next_command.rationale: Localization and mechanism are high-confidence and the implementation is a verified single-site replication of an established four-part pattern with no architectural fork to explore; the three open questions are scope and semantics decisions a spec can record as resolved, which is cheaper than a brainstorm.

meta.notes: Research completed well inside budget (12 files read, 9 greps, 1 git call against 40/25/10). The wiki's default store resolves to a stale docs/parrot/wiki.db and errors; --store .parrot/wiki works and was used throughout. Scope was widened at the Phase-1 gate on user request to survey the four other FEAT-397 holdout clients, which produced F008 and unknown U3. overall_confidence is bounded to medium by the median claim confidence (6 high / 6 medium), NOT by weak localization: every localization claim (C1-C5) is high-confidence and directly read. The medium claims are all peripheral scope judgments (C7-C12), which is why sdd-spec is still the right next command.
